headline: Asia had its worst week since 2020 overnight and chip stocks fell again before the open, but Treasuries finally rallied and the Dow held up: the selling is now concentrated in AI and chips.
summary: Levels below are Thursday Nov 19 closes from Massive unless marked intraday. About a quarter of the dashboard prices we checked (49 of 185) are still Wednesday closes, so use the numbers here, not the dashboard tiles (see the data signal). The S&P 500 ended its sixth straight loss at 7,175.83, down 5.1% for the week through Thursday. Overnight Taiwan fell 6.2% and Korea and Japan about 5%; AMD was down another 7% before the bell. The 10 year yield slipped under 5% and the VIX touched 31 early Friday, its highest since March (Reuters). In the first minutes of trading the Dow was up and the Nasdaq 100 down about 1% (intraday, not a close). Plan: no new swing entries; one put idea passed the screen (AEP Dec 18 120); no first pieces in chip names before ADI reports Tuesday.

regime.why: Six straight down days for the S&P 500, the longest run since April 2024 (Traders and Quants), and Asia's worst week since March 2020 (Reuters). The difference from Thursday: Treasuries rallied, with the 10 year under 5% for the first time this week, so bonds are cushioning stocks again. A December Fed hike is still priced as near certain.

signals.title: Asia's worst week since 2020, and this time bonds rallied
signals.since_yesterday: Taiwan fell 6.2% Friday and 17% for the week, its biggest weekly drop since 1990; the 10 year yield fell under 5% and the VIX hit 31, its highest since March (Reuters).
signals.what_happened: Friday in Asia: Taiwan's Taiex fell 6.2%, Korea's KOSPI 5.2% to 4,869.96 and Japan's Nikkei 5.1% to 56,436.65 (24/7 Wall St). MSCI's Asia Pacific index outside Japan fell 8% this week, its worst since March 2020, and Europe's STOXX 600 fell almost 2% (Reuters). Before the US open, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.6% to 2% while Dow futures were flat (24/7 Wall St; Reuters). Treasuries rallied: the 10 year yield fell for a fifth session to about 4.97% (Reuters), after Thursday's 5.04% close. In the first minutes of trading the S&P 500 was down about 0.2%, the Dow up about 0.5% and the Nasdaq 100 down about 1% (24/7 Wall St market bar, intraday only).
signals.so_what: Two things changed. The selling narrowed to chips and AI: the Dow, with few chip stocks, held while the Nasdaq 100 fell. And bonds worked as a hedge again, which Traders and Quants named as the test for whether balanced portfolios get relief. Who pays: Taiwan and Korea chip makers, and funds crowded in AI. Who gets paid: bond holders and the defensive groups. What would make this wrong: a seventh straight S&P 500 loss with yields rising again, which would be the longest losing run since the pandemic (Reuters).
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries until the S&P 500 has an up day on rising volume. WM (238.67) and DHR (227.56) sit within 0.3% of their stops; phone alerts are live at both stops and both triggers. Puts: richer premiums, but only outside chips; AEP passed today's screen. Long term: no first pieces in chip names until a close back over the point.

signals.title: AMD fell another 7% before the bell; ARK sold Nvidia and bought Anthropic in every fund
signals.since_yesterday: AMD traded at 454.80 before Friday's open, down 14.2% in two days from 530.14; ARK sold 33,430 NVDA shares from ARKQ on Thursday.
signals.what_happened: Before Friday's open AMD traded at 454.80, TSMC's US shares at 337.18 (down 4.2%, 31% under the October high), Micron down 4.8%, Intel 5.3%, Broadcom 2.9% and Nvidia 2.4%; the VanEck chip fund (SMH) was 35% under its June high (24/7 Wall St). Reuters tied the pressure to a short report on AMD's China ties, to Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia and to anti data center sentiment after the midterms. Anthropic was down about 10% before the open after closing its first day at 97.17 (Reuters). On Thursday ARK bought Anthropic in all six of its active funds and sold 33,430 Nvidia shares from ARKQ and 2,094 Eli Lilly shares from ARKG (ARK trade file). Thursday closes on the long term scan chip names (Massive): ANET 189.59, ADI 377.44, ENTG 138.14.
signals.so_what: The money rotating into the new AI lab is partly coming out of the AI hardware leaders, and the Asian supply chain is taking the hit. Second order: the suppliers that sell into the same build out (ANET, ENTG) have no reason to bounce until the leaders stop falling. What would make this wrong: ADI's report Tuesday showing industrial and auto demand holding up, which would split the analog names off from the AI trade.
signals.for_you: Long term: ANET is 1.6% under its 192.64 point, ADI 1.2% under 382.16 and ENTG 1.2% under 139.82; wait for a close back over the point. ADI reports Tuesday Nov 24 before the open (estimate $3.89 a share, Alpha Vantage), inside any December put, so no ADI put. AMD is off the long term buy list. No chip puts.

signals.title: The week in review: a 5% drop led by chips, insurers and a record IPO
signals.what_happened: Through Thursday the S&P 500 fell 5.1% for the week, six straight losses, and the Dow closed under 50,000 for the first time since June (24/7 Wall St; Traders and Quants). Four things drove it. Nvidia's beat could not hold: the stock fell Wednesday and Thursday to 145.98. The chip remote access rule took effect Nov 19 (Federal Register). CMS's CRUSH proposal to audit Medicare Advantage plans hit insurers: UNH fell from about 389.70 Tuesday to 330.48 Thursday, about 15%, with a confirmed range break on 3.15x volume (Massive; dashboard). Anthropic's $81 billion IPO pulled cash from other tech stocks (Traders and Quants). What held up: discount retail (Walmart beat and raised; WMT closed 126.04), utilities near their range tops (SO 93.29, DUK 128.86) and LMT over its long term point (571.85).
signals.so_what: This was a crowded trade unwinding, plus two policy shocks in one week, while the Fed is still set to hike. Breadth was poor (more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell Thursday, AP) but the losses were deepest in the most owned names. The defensive groups and discount retail are where money hid.
signals.for_you: Swing: the week cost the list two setups (MO void, TMO dropped Thursday); WM and DHR remain. Puts: the screen found one idea outside the falling groups (AEP). Long term: of 13 buy list names, 7 closed over their point and inside the zone Thursday (BLK, ABBV, AIN, PYPL, PFE, LMT, V); MA closed over its zone; the chip names, ACIW and AEP closed just under.

cycle.quadrant: Growth slowing while inflation stays high: late overheating, leaning toward stagflation
cycle.quadrant_why: No new growth or inflation data since Thursday's soft Philadelphia Fed survey and its jump in prices paid. The early November consumer sentiment read was 51.0 with year ahead inflation expectations at 4.3%; the final read comes today. The All Weather model is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A December quarter point hike is priced as nearly certain (Reuters), and the 10 year inflation protected note auction cleared at a 2.903% real yield, the highest at that auction since 2002 (Traders and Quants).
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Real yields near 3% on 10 year inflation protected notes make every dollar of debt costlier, and the government is hunting savings inside its own programs.
cycle.big_cycle: Technology and external order. The AI build out is being repriced from Taipei to New York in the same week a US chip export rule took effect. Internal order: the midterm result has added political pressure against data center expansion (Reuters).
tailwinds: Treasuries rallied on a down day, so bonds are cushioning stocks again.
Discount retail and utilities held up.
Oil is on track for a third weekly loss (Reuters).
headwinds: Asia's worst week since 2020 and Taiwan's since about 1990.
VIX at 31, the highest since March.
A Fed hike priced for December while growth slows.

history.when: August 5, 2024: Taiwan's worst day in 57 years
history.what: Taiwan's Taiex had its worst day in 57 years, led by TSMC, as a crowded trade (borrowed yen funding tech stocks) unwound worldwide. US stocks recovered within weeks once the Fed began cutting that September.
history.lesson: Forced selling in a crowded trade can end fast once the forced sellers are done, but the bounce needed a central bank that could ease.

source.title: BNN Bloomberg: TSMC leads Taiwan slump as index suffers worst day in 57 years (Aug 5, 2024)

cycle.differences: In 2024 the Fed was weeks from its first cut. Today it is weeks from a hike, and real yields are near 3%. The crowding is similar (AI hardware), but the cushion is thinner, so a fast V shaped recovery is less likely.
cycle.for_you: Swing: wait for an up day on rising volume; WM and DHR alerts are live. Puts: AEP Dec 18 120 passed; check the live bid. Long term: the seven names over their points can take small pieces; the chip names wait.

principle.text: Don't confuse what you wish were true with what is really true (paraphrase of Principles).
